draft.title: Factors that shift supply
card: A supply curve shows how much sellers will supply at each price. A change in the good's own price moves along the curve. A change in anything else shifts the whole curve.
Costs of production: if wages, rent or materials rise, selling is less profitable at each price. Supply falls and the curve shifts left. Lower costs shift it right.
Technology and productivity: better machines or methods let firms make more output from the same inputs, at a lower cost per unit. Supply rises and the curve shifts right.
The weather and other disruptions: a drought, flood, fire or strike can cut how much sellers can produce. Supply falls at each price and the curve shifts left.
draft.remember: Anything that changes the cost or ability to produce shifts the supply curve, not just the price.

a.q: A new machine lets a bakery in Ballarat bake more loaves from the same flour and labour. What happens to the supply of its bread?
opts: The supply curve shifts right
The supply curve shifts left
There is a movement up along the curve
There is a movement down along the curve
a.why: The machine raises productivity, so the bakery can supply more bread at every price. That shifts the whole curve right. A movement along the curve happens only when the bread's own price changes.
a.clue: Did the price of bread change, or did the bakery's ability to produce?

b.q: A flood destroys much of the tomato crop in a Victorian farming region. What is the effect on the supply curve for tomatoes?
opts: It shifts left, as less can be produced at each price
It shifts right, as tomatoes become scarcer and dearer
There is a movement along the curve to a higher price
There is a movement along the curve to a lower price
b.why: The flood cuts how much growers can produce, so they supply less at every price. That shifts the whole curve left. A movement along the curve would need a change in the tomato price to start it, but here the flood is the cause.
b.clue: The flood changes what growers can produce, not the price they are offered.

b.best: It shifts left, as less can be produced at each price

problems.detail: "Shifts the supply curve, not just the price" reads as though a change in the good's own price also shifts the curve. The card says a change in own price is a movement along the curve. Reword it, for example: "Anything other than the good's own price that changes the cost or ability to produce shifts the whole supply curve."

check.summary: Both questions are sound and their intended answers are correct. The remember line's "not just the price" wrongly suggests that a price change shifts the supply curve, which contradicts the card, so it should be reworded.
